subject: What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?

messages.author: b43184f1b55021fb
messages.subject: What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?
parts:
I could write a script that uses scp and ssh commands to transport the data to the server, run stan and then fetch the output back. But I would need to adjust the script each time when I want to run new simulation which is cumbersome.

I was looking at Ipython's parallel computing functionality. It looks great. I like how it handles the data transport automatically. But I'm not sure how well it works with PyStan. Does CmdStan provide some functionality for parallel distributed processing?

I'm curious, what are you people using to run Stan on remote servers?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?
parts:
Hi,

CmdStan does not provide functionality for parallel distributed processing. But, it's the right option if you want to run on a cluster where you don't need a computing framework to interactively look at results.

I've managed to do what you've described using some clever scripting on a cluster.


Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?
parts:
Hi Matus,

I sync with rsync (via ssh, you can automate it), and I run a remote
R session with ESS, and use rstan.

That said, I only use the server for computationally intensive models,
and even then I always refine the model on my laptop first. For my
models, the compilation to C++ and some benchmarking with about 20
iterations are not that time-consuming.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: ffa9d79601717d80
messages.subject: What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?
parts: If you want to use RStudio, then install RStudio Server on the server, set up an SSH tunnel, and use the browser version of RStudio. That works much more smoothly then using an ordinary RStudio instance with X11.

messages.author: b43184f1b55021fb
messages.subject: Re: What is the recommended way of running Stan on a remote server?
parts:
Thanks for input everyone!

I have three i7 machines (servers) and my desktop pc (also i7). The servers don't have X11 nor in fact any DE installed. Even if they had, it is inconvenient for me to setup stan simulation each time with remote desktop. I would run two 6 chain simulations in parallel per machine. Say I want to do 8 simulations. The simulations don't take long, but it does make difference whether they run 12 minutes (single machine) or 3 minutes (all 4 machines). Furthermore the machines have only single 128GB ssd drive (half of it set up as memory swap) and I can't afford to keep my whole data stack on each server with rsync.

So I'm looking for a solution that handles all my (say 8) simulations across all 4 machines including the data transfer with a single command. I'm going to investigate ipython some more. I'm afraid ipython uses pickle dumps to transfer the data and I'm not sure how well pystan supports pickling.

Ideally, I would love to have a stan controller that is fed a set of models, datasets and instructions about how to match the two and how many chains to run in each case. One would also provide info about the servers - how many machines and how many jobs/chains can be run in parrallel on each. Then  the controller goes to the servers and distributes all chains such that each machine is under full load until all jobs are assigned.

Daniel are your scripts available online? Would you mind to share them? I hope they don't use some esoteric cluster scripting language.
